200.description: Bootstrap config; update.decision is none|recommended|required, where required comes from updatePolicy.minSupportedVersion or from a mandatory active release. wallet.tokens lists the token catalogue for the app (BootstrapWalletToken[]): only enabled tokens on the tenant's enabled chains, tenant rows override global rows with the same (chain, address), sorted by sortWeight DESC then symbol ASC; it never carries verified/id/scope (the app grants verified from its own allowlist). wallet.tokens is required by the app schema; every enabled chain carries an enabled native entry, and every delivered row is validated before delivery (a corrupt row makes the whole bootstrap fail with 503 rather than being repaired on the read path); services.predict (domain, scopeId, chain) is present only while modules.predict is enabled and is 503 when enabled but not configured. Optional installation authentication: a request carrying X-Installation-ID plus Authorization: Installation <credential> is matched against canary releases, so the device may receive update.full/update.ota for a canary build instead of the active one; an absent, expired or revoked credential is treated as anonymous and only ever sees active (bootstrap itself never fails on a credential problem). update.canary.enrolled says whether the offered full release is a canary build; update.canary.otaToken is a 24h opaque token that the app must store with Updates.setExtraParamAsync("canary-token", token) so the native manifest request can be matched to a canary OTA revision (the key must stay lowercase: expo-structured-headers rejects uppercase dictionary keys). otaToken is null when the installation could not be authenticated, and the app then clears the stored param. update.minSupportedVersion and the mandatory flag always come from the active release, never from a canary one features.directUpdateEnabled is additionally false when the requesting build and the release it would install were signed with different certificates (the platform installer would reject the in-app install after the download), so the client falls back to opening the download URL instead of looping a failing install.

503.description: BOOTSTRAP_UNAVAILABLE: the tenant configuration, its token catalogue or its wallet section could not be produced completely (storage error, a corrupt catalogue row, an enabled chain without a native token, or a tenant whose configured chains are all unknown). The app keeps its last successful snapshot and shows the retry screen

The certificate must match the private key: a mismatch would make every device silently reject updates and stay on the embedded bundle, so it is refused at write time. Signatures are emitted as the RFC 8941 `expo-signature` dictionary (sig/keyid/alg=rsa-v1_5-sha256) over the final response bytes.

The certificate carries X509v3 Key Usage: Digital Signature and Extended Key Usage: Code Signing, which is exactly what expo-updates' CertificateChain checks; NotBefore is backdated five minutes because the client validates against the device clock. An OTA job is refused when the tenant has no OTA signing key, when the base release carries no runtimeVersion, or when another OTA job for the same tenant and platform is still in flight (OTA_BUILD_ALREADY_QUEUED) - the queue is shared across tenants and OTA jobs have no build-number monotonicity to limit them. channel is never taken from the request: it is compiled into the base APK, so it comes from the tenant's composed identity. An android apk job is refused with 409 SIGNER_NOT_READY unless the primary signer is ready for this tenant; after changing apiBaseUrl or the OTA key it stays refused until the primary signer re-confirms.

APP_IDENTITY_DRIFT: this build would change the Android package name or signing certificate of the active release, so installed devices cannot upgrade in place; the detail is written for people - after the operator confirms, resend the same request with acknowledgeIdentityChange=true. SIGNER_NOT_READY (android apk): the primary signer cannot sign for this tenant yet - no v3 keystore, keystore not sealed to the primary, trust roots cannot be composed (no OTA certificate), or the primary has not decrypted, confirmed (with the current trust roots digest) and trial-signed the current keystore version; the detail lists what is missing and the problem body carries readinessProblems (SignerReadinessProblem[]). Otherwise claiming increments signAttempt, deletes any signed package left by a previous sign attempt and moves the job to signing. keyAlias and trustRoots are for comparison only. A job this signer deferred (POST /jobs/{id}/release, signOutcome.kind=deferred with this machine's id) is not dispatched to the same signer again until 60 seconds after signOutcome.at; other signers are not affected.

post.summary: Complete signing: create the release and finish the job atomically
post.description: Outside the transaction the server reads the signed package back from storage (the key recorded by the last signed upload of this claim) and runs the same release checks as a manual upload: signer certificate = registered keystore certificate = certificateSha256, package name, versionName/versionCode = job, not the public debug key, not a retired certificate; unsignedSha256 must match the builder delivery and nativeFingerprint must equal the value from the builder's verified provenance (422 SIGN_RESULT_MISMATCH otherwise; the package does not carry it, so the release records the job's value with file_metadata.nativeFingerprintSource = builder-provenance). The signing heartbeat is refreshed before the download so a long verification is not reaped. Then, under the release sequence lock, one transaction locks the job row, checks status/signAttempt/machine, checks that the signed object key is still the one that was verified (409 SIGNED_ARTIFACT_REPLACED when the package was uploaded again meanwhile: call complete again) that the signer has not been revoked meanwhile (401 MACHINE_REVOKED), and re-reads release.android and build.keystore with a shared lock: if the registered package name, certificate or keystore changed after the verification the completion is refused (409 RELEASE_IDENTITY_CHANGED, audited as release_rejected; call complete again), checks that version and build number increase, inserts app_releases (status verified, file_metadata adds unsignedSha256, sbom, nativeFingerprint, nativeFingerprintSource, commitSha, commitSelfReported, buildJobId, builderId, signerMachineId), marks the job succeeded with release_id and artifact_sha256, and audits as system-signer. Idempotent: a succeeded job with the same signed sha256, the same signAttempt and the same signer machine returns the same releaseId; the same signer and attempt with a different signedSha256 gets 409 SIGN_RESULT_CONFLICT (the recorded release is not replaced); any other signer or attempt gets 409 SIGN_ATTEMPT_STALE. Exempt from the database timeout by exact route match.

claimedBy.description: Builder name from the machine registry

commitSelfReported.description: Always true: the commit is reported by the builder and not verified by the server.

publicKey.description: Standard base64 of the 32-byte Ed25519 provenance public key

rotationSignature.description: Required when the machine is already active and reports a different key: standard base64 Ed25519 signature by the CURRENT key over machinekey.RotationMessage(machineId, sha256(newKey), "")

x25519PublicKey.description: Standard base64, 32 bytes; its sha256 is the keystore recipient fingerprint

ed25519PublicKey.description: Standard base64, 32 bytes; signs the local records and key rotations

rotationSignature.description: Required when the signer is already active and reports different keys: Ed25519 signature by the current ed25519 key over machinekey.RotationMessage(machineId, sha256(x25519), sha256(ed25519))

machineId.description: This machine's registry id; signed into machinekey.RotationMessage when rotating keys

MachineKeyStatus.description: Every sha256 is computed over the raw 32-byte public key (base64-decoded), lowercase hex.

statement.description: Standard base64 of the raw JSON bytes of the rn-build-provenance v1 statement (signing/provenance)

signature.description: Standard base64 Ed25519 signature over "rn-build-provenance/v1\n" || statement bytes

sha256.description: Computed by the server while receiving the stream

KeystoreBox.description: A v3 keystore ciphertext sealed to one signer (signing/keystorebox). The server cannot open it.

recipientSha256.description: sha256 of the recipient signer X25519 public key

KeystoreUpload.description: The file produced by the offline build-keystore tool, sealed only to the signers in the offline pin file.

TrustRoots.description: Trust roots compiled into the package (signing/trustroots), composed by the server from the tenant manifest and the current OTA certificate. Signers only use them for comparison; they confirm their own values locally.

configured.description: A v3 record is stored (even one that cannot be used; see readinessProblems KEYSTORE_RECORD_INVALID)

legacy.description: The stored row is a retired format (passphrase or build-agent box); it counts as not configured and must be replaced

missingSigners.description: Active signers the keystore is not sealed to (a hint, not an error)

ready.description: Same judgement as the queue gate (SIGNER_NOT_READY) and the signer claim

readinessProblems.description: Why the tenant is not ready, in check order; an empty array when ready is true

MachineView.description: Registry entry without the token digest and without raw public keys.

signerRole.description: Signers only: primary or standby. null for builders and for revoked signers (cleared on revoke).

reportedLocalRole.description: Signers only: the role this signer last reported from its own local record (POST /v1/signer/keystore-checks localRole). null = never reported. The console's signerRole only routes; when they differ on the primary, tenants are not ready.

reportedLocalRoleAt.description: When reportedLocalRole last changed; null = never reported

publicKeySha256.description: Full 64-hex sha256 read on the machine itself (colons and upper case accepted)

ed25519PublicKeySha256.description: Required when the machine is a signer (400 INVALID_MACHINE without it): the full 64-hex sha256 of the signer's Ed25519 key read on the signer itself (colons and upper case accepted), which must equal the pending Ed25519 key (409 MACHINE_KEY_MISMATCH). Checking only the X25519 fingerprint would let a stolen token pair the real X25519 key with a foreign Ed25519 key while the machine is pending. Builders have a single key: leave it out (any value is 409 MACHINE_KEY_MISMATCH).

keyAlias.description: For comparison only; the signer uses the alias inside the box

localRole.description: This signer's role according to its own local record (signer promote/abandon). Required on every report. Stored on the machine as reportedLocalRole/reportedLocalRoleAt, written only when it changes; a routed primary whose reportedLocalRole is not primary makes tenants not ready (PRIMARY_SIGNER_LOCAL_ROLE_MISMATCH).

nativeFingerprint.description: Must equal the nativeFingerprint of the builder's verified provenance recorded on the job

SignerReadinessProblem.description: One reason the primary signer cannot sign for this tenant yet. code is a fixed enum the console maps to a fix-it entry; detail is a human sentence that may name a machine or quote the signer's error. KEYSTORE_NOT_CONFIGURED: no build.keystore. KEYSTORE_LEGACY_FORMAT: build.keystore is a pre-signing-gate record (v1 passphrase box or v2 build-agent box); reset and upload v3. KEYSTORE_RECORD_INVALID: build.keystore is a v3 record that cannot be used (the record is malformed, the outer box cannot be opened, or its index fields differ from the stored upload); the keystore view still reports configured=true, the queue gate answers SIGNER_NOT_READY and the signer keystore checks omit the tenant - upload the v3 file again. RELEASE_IDENTITY_NOT_CONFIGURED / RELEASE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH: release.android is missing or differs from the keystore's package name or certificate. PRIMARY_SIGNER_MISSING: no active primary signer is registered. PRIMARY_SIGNER_NOT_RECIPIENT: the v3 keystore has no box for the primary signer. PRIMARY_SIGNER_LOCAL_ROLE_MISMATCH: the primary signer in the console has never reported its local role or its local record still says standby (it was not promoted on the machine), so it will not claim jobs; promote it on the machine or switch the console back. APP_IDENTITY_INCOMPLETE: tenant.json cannot be composed (missing app parameters, bootstrap signer address, release identity). OTA_CERTIFICATE_NOT_CONFIGURED: no ota.signing, so trust roots cannot be composed. API_BASE_URL_INVALID: the stored apiBaseUrl is not a canonical https origin (e.g. an explicit :443 saved before write-time validation). TRUST_ROOTS_INVALID: the composed trust roots do not normalize (e.g. scheme http/https). PRIMARY_SIGNER_NOT_CHECKED: the primary has not reported a check for the current keystore version. PRIMARY_SIGNER_DECRYPT_FAILED: its trial decryption failed. PRIMARY_SIGNER_NOT_CONFIRMED: not confirmed on the machine (signer confirm). TRUST_ROOTS_CHANGED: confirmed, but with a trust roots digest that is no longer current. PRIMARY_SIGNER_TRIAL_SIGN_PENDING / PRIMARY_SIGNER_TRIAL_SIGN_FAILED: the trial signing has not passed yet / failed.

tenantDirectory.description: Directory under RN-App tenants/ (build.android repoDirectory, defaults to the slug)

tenantFile.description: tenant.json composed by the server for this job: slug, appName, scheme, androidPackage, iosBundleId, apiBaseUrl, bootstrapSignerAddress, applicationId, distributionChannel, otaChannel, version, androidVersionCode, iosBuildNumber, iconBackgroundColor, icon{icon,androidForeground,androidBackground,androidMonochrome}, signerSha256

icons.description: Icon file names to fetch one by one with GET /v1/build-agent/jobs/{id}/icons/{name}

googleServicesJson.description: base64 google-services.json, or null when not configured

otaCertificatePem.description: Public OTA code-signing certificate compiled into the package (null when ota.signing is not configured); the private key is never sent

runtimeVersion.description: OTA jobs only: the base release's runtimeVersion

claimedMachineId.description: This builder's machine id; use it as the provenance builderId

attempt.description: Send it as x-build-attempt on every /jobs/{id}/* request

BuilderClaimResponse.description: A claimed job. No keystore material of any kind is included.
